children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Losses in Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were getting softer Thursday due to increases in crude oil.
There's pressure on canola coming from losses in Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil. Chicago soybeans and soymeal were moving higher, providing spillover support.
An analyst said it's unlikely canola will stay down for the rest of Thursday's session.
"We should gain some strength from oil," he said.
Even with the losses in canola, its November contract remained above its major moving averages.
Canola crush margins fell back with the November positions giving up about C$9 to C$10, placing them between C$273.50 to C$282.10 per tonne above the futures.
Saskatchewan is set to issue its weekly crop report later Thursday. Manitoba said its canola harvest was 5% complete.
Field operations on the Prairies will be limited Thursday, as much of the much region is to get rain. Depending on location, temperatures are to range from the high teens to upper 20 degrees Celsius.
The Canadian dollar was exploiting weakness in its U.S. counterpart late Thursday morning. The loonie rose to 72.54 U.S. cents, compared with Wednesday's close of 72.13.
